actions.description: Advance the simulated world by a bounded number of fixed timesteps, optionally applying an action for each step, and return the resulting observation and terminal flags.

inputs.description: Transitions to advance; the action is applied at every tick
inputs.name: ticks

inputs.description: The action applied at each tick, shaped by the environment's action space
inputs.name: action

actions.name: step

actions.description: Reset the simulated world to a scenario start state and return the initial observation. When a seed is supplied the endpoint records it in the receipt; otherwise the endpoint's declared default seed applies.

inputs.description: Accepted for the class contract; a MuJoCo reset restores the model defaults (mj_resetData) and does not use a seed
inputs.name: seed

actions.name: reset

facts.text: The repository provides URDF, MuJoCo MJCF and USD robot descriptions for the LimX HU_D03 and HU_D04 humanoids, for ROS, MuJoCo and NVIDIA Isaac Sim.
The README's available-models table names HU_D03_03.xml and HU_D04_01.xml as the MuJoCo MJCF files for HU_D03 and HU_D04.
The README marks HU_D03 as discontinued and says to use HU_D04 instead.
The MuJoCo quick start runs python -m mujoco.viewer with HU_D04_description/xml/HU_D04_01.xml.
The HU_D03 package README names HU_D03_description/xml/HU_D03_03.xml as its MJCF.
The HU_D04 package README names HU_D04_description/xml/HU_D04_01.xml as its MJCF.

The HU_D03 CMakeLists installs the meshes, urdf, xml and world directories into the ROS package share for ROS 1 and ROS 2, or into etc/ when only AMENT_PREFIX_PATH is set; it defines no executable target.
The HU_D03 CMakeLists header reads '© [2025] LimX Dynamics Technology Co., Ltd. All rights reserved.'

The HU_D03 package manifest names HU_D03_description, leaves its licence field as TODO, declares catkin/ament build types with roscpp/rclcpp dependencies, and declares no message, service or action definition.
The README's licence section names the Apache License 2.0 and the LICENSE file.
The HU_D03 MJCF root element declares the model name HU_D03_03.
The HU_D03 MJCF compiler sets angle='radian' and meshdir='../meshes/HU_D03_03/'.
The HU_D03 MJCF sets its integration timestep to 0.001 s.
The HU_D03 base body base_link is placed at pos='0 0 1.0' and carries the free joint floating_base_joint.
The left_hip_pitch_joint is a hinge joint limited to -3.1415 to 3.1415 rad with armature 0.15257125.
The actuator section declares motors for the legs, waist, head, arms and hands, and every motor sets ctrllimited='true' with an explicit ctrlrange.
The hip and knee motor ctrlranges are -120 to 120 and the ankle motor ctrlranges are -45 to 45.
The waist motor ctrlranges are -45 to 45 and the head motor ctrlranges are -18 to 18.
The left arm motor ctrlranges are -30 to 30 for the shoulder and elbow motors and -18 to 18 for the wrist and hand motors.
The right arm motor ctrlranges are -30 to 30 for the shoulder and elbow motors and -18 to 18 for the wrist and hand motors.

determinism.notes: The stand-in is deterministic, but its placeholder motion is not the engine's physics; cap.world.reset.v1 restores zeros and takes no seed.

gaps: the fake backend is a stand-in for the mujoco library, not MuJoCo: it reads the MJCF for the joint dimensions and the per-motor ctrlranges, and integrates a placeholder torque-like motion: each motor's control value accelerates its joint through a placeholder gain against a placeholder damping, with no inertia, gravity, contact, joint limit or equality constraint, so trajectories, actuator dynamics and the free-base dynamics are not MuJoCo's
the stand-in moves each motor's own joint; the ankle and waist motors drive rod joints whose linkage to the ankle and waist is a set of connect equality constraints that the stand-in does not resolve

the stand-in derives qpos0 from the MJCF text (the free joint at the base_link pose 0 0 1.0 with an identity quaternion, identity quaternions for the six ball joints, zero for every hinge) and restores it on reset, but it runs no mj_forward and resolves no constraint, so the reset pose is not settled by physics
the fake has no mj_getState/mj_setState/mj_stateSize, so the bridge uses its basic checkpoint profile: time, qpos, qvel, ctrl and actuator activation are restored, not MuJoCo's full integration state
no mesh or texture is loaded by the stand-in, and no backend exposes the model's IMU site, joint-position sensors or force/torque sensors
no rendering is offered; the bridge exposes qpos, qvel, ctrl and time, not the model's camera or sensor arrays
the package serves the card's models[0] only; the HU_D04 model (models[1]), which the README recommends because HU_D03 is discontinued, is not served

the upstream is a description repository with no controller executable, ROS node, topic, service or action; this package drives the bare MJCF plant with raw motor torques, not a deployed robot, a controller or a ROS graph, so the humanoid falls unless a caller supplies balancing torques
no physical HU_D03 robot is modelled or driven; this simulated package has no hardware backend and nothing was validated against hardware

measures.description: Declared native checkpoint. Integration profile restores the full native input vector; basic profile restores only advertised state plus actuator activation and exact native time. Neither profile certifies external callbacks, plugins, RNG or hardware fidelity.
measures.name: native_checkpoint

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step or reset is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the integration state is kept and stays readable
